coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Each lateral frame cropped from the full scan at 1.5-2x (hip region at 3-4x) with a grid labelled in scan pixels and raised contrast. Joint points are estimated joint centres, not skin landmarks: shoulder = centre of the humeral head under the deltoid; hip = greater trochanter, taken about 25-35 px in from the rear contour of the buttock at the level of the thigh's midline (the least certain point, about +-10 px); knee = centre of the knee between its front and back contours; ankle = centre of the malleolus; toe = tip of the foot; heel = back of the heel; head = top of the skull (crown). Every point set was drawn back onto its crop (dots + segments) and corrected until it sat on the joint; only points that passed are kept. Angles are computed by atan2 from these points; with a +-10 px hip, segment angles carry about +-5 deg. Heights are 'ground y minus point y' in scan pixels, with each frame's own ground (the sole line of the planted feet), because every frame comes from a different camera and the floor line differs by a few pixels between frames. The man faces LEFT, so 'forward' is -x: trunk lean, 'ahead of hip' and thigh angles are signed for a left-facing figure (positive = forward). 'Near' leg = the one that occludes the other at the knee (it overlaps the other thigh); 'far' = the other. In the seated frames the near thigh points partly towards the camera (knees spread; see the front row), so its projected length is 72-88 px against 114-130 px for the far thigh: near-leg angles are foreshortened and only far-leg angles are used for findings. Lengths are normalised by the standing hip height L = 236 px (frame 1).
frameBoxesNote: lateral (top) row only, listed by source frame 1-12; frame 1 is the RIGHTMOST box (numbers handwritten bottom left of each frame, read 12 ... 2 from left to right). Edges +-10 px.

findings: Frame numbering checked on the full scan: the lateral row is numbered 1-12 from RIGHT to LEFT (12 is the leftmost box), so the action does run right to left: frame 1 standing at the right, frame 12 seated at the left. The man faces left.

The plate's 2.0 s is the whole action, most of it walking in and placing the chair (frames 1-6). The sit-down itself (end of the step back to seated) is frames 7-10: 0.55 s (3 intervals), at most 0.73 s if it starts at frame 6. The hip drop is front-loaded: 22 of the 47 px from frame 7 to 12 happen in the first interval (frame 7 to 8), then 5-7 px per interval, within the +-10 px hip error; the crown drops 35, 27 and 13 px over frames 7-10 and then holds.

Hip height: standing 236 px; seated 158-165 px (frames 11-12) = 0.67-0.70 of standing hip height, i.e. the hips drop about 0.3-0.33 L on to this chair. (If L is taken from segment lengths, thigh 124 + shank 107 + ankle 23 = 254 px, the seated ratio is 0.63-0.65; the true value lies in 0.63-0.70.)

Trunk: the hip-shoulder line stays within 3-13 deg of vertical (forward) throughout; the largest lean is at the start of the descent (frame 8, 12.6 deg), seated 4.5-6 deg. The visible 'bend' in frames 9-10 is head and shoulders rounding forward (crown 93-103 px ahead of the hip) with the hands going to the knees, not a hip hinge.

Seated pose (frames 11-12, far leg): knee 95-97 deg interior (about 85 deg flexion), hip (trunk-thigh) 98-102 deg interior, thigh 14-16 deg BELOW horizontal (knee lower than hip). Shank nearly vertical (ankle 10-20 px in front of the knee).

Feet: the far foot stays flat on the floor in front, toe 0.62-0.67 L ahead of the hip in every frame from 8 to 12; the near foot is drawn back under the chair, toe roughly below the hip (-0.06 to +0.19 L), on the ball of the foot with the heel 13-23 px up. Both feet stay on the floor.

Comparison with figures/human.json motions.sit (a looping seated idle on an edge: 12 frames @ 6 fps = 2.0 s, lower 19, legsForward 20, legsUp 23, kick 2; posed with `pixel where human --anim sit`): standing hip height in our figure is 41.5 units (hip y 52, foot line 93.5). lower 19 puts the seated hip at 0.54 L; on this chair the hip sits at 0.63-0.70 L, i.e. lower = 13-15 units for a chair-height seat with the feet on the floor. Our seated toe is 26 units (0.63 L) ahead of the hip, which matches the plate's front foot (0.62-0.67 L) - but ours hangs 4 units above the foot line and swings (kick 2), while the plate's feet are planted, one forward and one tucked back. Our thigh rises 15 deg above horizontal (knee 5 units above the hip, from legsUp) with hip interior about 69 deg and knee interior about 81 deg; the plate has the thigh 14-16 deg below horizontal, hip about 100 deg and knee about 96 deg. So our pose reads as 'perched on a ledge, knees up' (fine for an edge sit), not chair sitting. The 2.0 s match noted in docs/research/motion-references.md (plate 2.0 s vs our 2.0 s loop) is a coincidence: the plate's 2.0 s is the whole chair-placing action; the sit-down is 0.55-0.73 s.

A one-shot 'sit down' transition, from this plate: about 0.55-0.75 s (4-5 frames at 6-8 fps; this plate is 5.5 fps). Start: step back so one foot is under the seat; first interval drops the hips quickly (about half the drop from the step-back pose) with the trunk tipped about 10-13 deg forward and the hands moving to the knees; then the hips ease down the rest over 2-3 intervals while the head and shoulders round forward over the knees; end with the trunk back to about 5 deg, hips at 0.63-0.70 L, knee about 95 deg, front foot flat at about 0.65 L ahead of the hip and the other foot tucked under with the heel up. Ease-out (fast then slow), not linear.

Not measured: the chair seat height and the moment the buttocks touch the seat (the seat is hidden behind the body in frames 8-12); hip points in frames 2-4 (only seen at 1.5x, standing walk while carrying the chair, not needed for the sit); near-leg angles in seated frames (foreshortened, see method); any lateral (sideways) motion - the front-view row was not measured; world positions across frames (each frame is a different camera).
